title: How airlines really make money (it isn't the seats)
description:
You think an airline sells seats. Its most valuable product is the points on your credit card.
Rohan books a flight and follows his money: the thin profit on the seat, the fare ladder, the fees, the cargo under his feet, the miles banks buy by the billion, and the loyalty programme that can be worth more than the airline itself.
Then the question nobody asks: who actually pays for all those free flights?
